Params: NORTHERN WATERS, TRANSATLANTIC ECONOMIC COMMUNITY TERRITORY
LOCATION: KURONO VESSEL, SHIP CABIN. NORTHERN WATERS, TRANSATLANTIC ECONOMIC COMMUNITY TERRITORY.
A violent shudder rises from somewhere deep below, throwing Clausen from his seat. The lights choke and sputter.
By the time the power stabilizes and the cabin floods with light again, she is no longer sitting. She is standing over him.
Wh-what do you think you're doing?!
Just offering a hand, Captain Clausen.
I can stand on my own! Sit back down, Lieutenant Colonel!

Clausen bats aside the hand Adelyde offers him and straightens up, his composure visibly shaken. Without a moment's pause, he jabs the comm channel open and snarls into it, demanding an explanation for the tremor.
Captain, the ship just took a direct hit from a massive wave. Source appears to be large-scale current displacement across the area. Most likely a chain reaction from the Balder's operations.
The Balder? That ship is carrying elite forces. Gray Raven's on board, for god's sake. What are they even doing out there?
No official briefing has come through yet, sir. But based on their encrypted comms, they're running a full sweep of the undersea cables and replacing faulty relay stations node by node.
All this chaos just to patch up some cables? And speaking of which, wasn't it right after Gray Raven filed that report on Port Podesta that the Red Tide started pouring into the ocean?

That settles it. That commandant must have screwed up the mission and conveniently left it out of the report. It's not the first time, either. Every time that one shows up somewhere, things spiral out of control.
Gray Raven's commandant would never do that.
Oh, here we go. The instructor's old habits kicking in. Playing favorites with your own student?

Question my actions or my loyalties all you like. But Gray Raven's commandant does not withhold intelligence. When things fall apart on the ground, it has never been a question of that person's competence.
It's because Gray Raven gets deployed to the worst battlefields where no one can predict how things will turn, where the situation is already at its breaking point.
A quiet fury threads through Adelyde's voice, and her stare cuts into Clausen like honed steel.

Something coils tight inside his chest. He understands, with sudden and visceral certainty, that this disarmed lieutenant colonel standing captive before him could crush him without effort if she wished it.
Pushing any further would be an act of self-humiliation.
Hmph. We'll set that aside for now. Lieutenant Colonel, the surviving Sirens' coordinates you submitted are accurate, I assume?

They're accurate. You should have my submersible in your possession as well. Use my identification code, and you'll also be able to pull up the locations of Moses' gravitational field manipulation devices.
You heard her. Adjust course and prep the salvage gear.

Once the orders are set, the tightness in Clausen's face relaxes just a fraction. The upper hand is his again. He leans forward, palms pressing flat against the tabletop, and delivers his next question like a card he has been waiting to play.
Earlier, you said the moment you linked the Siren into the master AI, you heard someone call out to you. What exactly happened there?

It called my surname, not me personally. Given the circumstances, only the master AI could have reached me through that channel. And its creator, the person who initiated the entire Millennium Project, was indeed a Helio.
The person who initiated the project... Let me pull that up.
With a wave of his hand, Clausen brings the holographic display to life. He navigates to the Millennium Project dossier, the public version his superiors handed down before the mission began.
Millennium Project General Director: Dale Helio. According to this, he was a lean man, just under six-foot-five.
Clausen taps through to the profile of the project director. A team photo sits on the page, taken in the early days of the Millennium Project.
The photograph earns a faint raise of Adelyde's brow. She has seen it before. The Babylonia operator pulled it up for her back before the mission.
He flips to the page listing the core team. A photograph taken at the project's inception stares back.

Four lead researchers, three men and one woman, one from each of the four great families. Together, they capture the concentrated brilliance of a bygone era, the scientific might of the Transatlantic Economic Community made flesh.

Their differences leap from the image. The Spelmin engineer is rigid and solemn, a man carved from discipline. At the center, the Erhorn researcher wears his arrogance like a coat of arms, ambition burning in his eyes.
The Copperfield scholar stands apart with a gentle serenity that tempers the group's sharp edges.

And then, at last, there is Helio. He wears a simple formal suit, his eyes unreadable behind thick lenses. A ghost of a smile rests on his lips, distant and knowing. The tall and composed man draws the eye without effort, a presence that refuses to be ignored.

Dale Helio. Started in engineering, then shifted toward research on the origins of life. While everyone else was looking up at the stars, he kept insisting on looking down, searching for the primordial soup that sparked life on Earth...
After skimming through a few pages of dry research history and confirming that Adelyde has not been lying, Clausen loses all patience for reading any further.
So if the master AI reached out, that means you've already found where it is?
I have. But finding it triggered an explosion. Yes, Captain, the very same explosion you saw. The one I caused.
What? That explosion is tied to the master AI? Don't tell me you blasted the thing!
The explosion happened at a different node. The one that can actually reach the master AI...
...is the independent undersea data center operated by the Erhorn family. The Netherweb.
NORTHERN WATERS, TRANSATLANTIC ECONOMIC COMMUNITY TERRITORY, DEPTH: 600 METERS
SOMETIME EARLIER. LOCATION: NORTHERN WATERS, TRANSATLANTIC ECONOMIC COMMUNITY TERRITORY. DEPTH: 600 METERS.

The ocean floor stretched on in empty silence. The fish were gone now, as if the sea itself had whispered a warning and they had listened. All that remained was the bone-white coral, a graveyard of color that marked where life used to be.

The master AI offered nothing more after that single question. A set of coordinates followed, delivered in silence. Almost at the same moment, a second message flickered onto Adelyde's terminal, an order to rendezvous with a Kurono ship.
She left it read but unanswered. Restarting her submersible, she turned toward the coordinates instead.
They guided her to the perimeter of the Netherweb undersea data center. Unlike the crumbling ruin of the Moses base, this facility stood sealed and silent, its secrets locked tight within.
Every visible entry point and viewing port had been sealed shut, barricaded behind heavy alloy plating. No ordinary entrance remained.
Just as the impasse began to feel absolute, she discovered a surveillance terminal tucked into a corner of the outer perimeter that still offered an access port she could use.
The data's pushed back to me?

The instant the terminal linked up, information began pouring backward into the submersible's databanks. Node archives, operational logs, foundational records, all of it flooding in at once until the Netherweb's full picture lay unlocked before her.

Adelyde now understood what she was looking at. The Netherweb was Erhorn's creation, a sprawling undersea data center built from countless server stations scattered across the ocean floor and threaded together by proprietary fiber-optic lines. It was a private deep-sea network, purpose-built for the Millennium Project.
And because the data it held was so sensitive and the project so unstable, Erhorn had installed one final safeguard: a physical deadlock that could seal the entire Netherweb shut.

According to its preset protocols, the moment the system detected severe interference, an intrusion attempt, or a viral threat, alloy barriers would automatically seal every entrance. It was a total physical lockout, designed to let nothing through.

When the Punishing Virus broke out, and its corruption bled into the surrounding nodes, the Netherweb responded instantly, throwing every barrier down at once and entombing itself in the state that Adelyde now found it.

So these alloy barriers are the physical locks. The system can trigger them to drop, but once they're down, the linkage mechanisms seize up completely. Even if I break through the system permissions, I still can't unlock the entrances remotely.
Which means the only way in is to force my way through.
NORTHERN WATERS, TRANSATLANTIC ECONOMIC COMMUNITY TERRITORY, DEPTH: 600 METERS
SOMETIME EARLIER. LOCATION: INSIDE THE NETHERWEB DATA CENTER. NORTHERN WATERS, TRANSATLANTIC ECONOMIC COMMUNITY TERRITORY. DEPTH: 600 METERS.
A deep, concussive blast ripped open the silence of the undersea chamber. For a brief moment, the space was nothing but churning smoke and the clatter of shredded metal raining down.
And then, through the haze, came calm footsteps. They crossed the wrecked threshold and began to resonate through the empty hall of dead servers.
Breaching here keeps the flooding manageable. But just as I thought... it's the same as Moses. Most of the equipment's in low-power hibernation.

The lights in the server room still clung to life, though barely. They cast only a weak, sickly glow across the space. Silence and decay filled every corner, and it was obvious that the data center had been dying for a long time.
No sign anyone's been through here... So who sent me that data?
从接收到物理锁的信息开始，阿德莱德就开始警戒起来，毕竟系统本身并不会对入侵者做这种“欢迎仪式”。

Yet after scouring the chamber, she found nothing but cold machinery and silence. The place was empty of life. She made her way to the central terminal and began sifting through the archives stored in the server array.
Somewhere in those files, she felt certain, the answer was waiting.
To date, this deep-sea exploration initiative has cataloged over thirty thousand new marine species.
The deeper we descend, the clearer it becomes that humanity's understanding of this planet is staggeringly narrow.
To study these lifeforms, the Netherweb node has concurrently conducted artificial cultivation and data modeling experiments, yielding numerous landmark research achievements.
This data was made possible because...
...shortly after the project's inception, "Copperfield" proactively offered additional project support, expanding the Netherweb far beyond its original scope.
This node was not the only one to receive such aid.
To accelerate undersea base construction, most of the Moses node's work machinery was manufactured by "Spelmin", simply rebranded prior to inspection.
After deftly evading the Community Council's scrutiny, the lead researchers gathered here to take the project's first group photo.
That's right. The same one included as an appendix in the public dossier. Since you've made it this far, I assume you've seen it.
A sudden intensity flickered behind Adelyde's gaze. The terminal's voice had shifted, its sterile cadence falling away to reveal something that sounded almost alive.
She knew then, without any doubt, that the hidden hand directing her steps and supplying her with information had been this very system all along. The Netherweb itself.
在先前的连接中，我反向读取了你的终端，得知了你来到这里之前见到了什么，也得知这片海域上面发生了什么。
我需要你帮我完成一件事，一件连接主脑之前，必须了结的隐患。
You can ask, but I can't promise I can deliver.
You can. I need you to destroy every branch server room in the other nodes. All of them except mine.
The virus you call Punishing has corrupted the entire project. And as the data center, I appear to be its primary target.
I triggered the defense protocols as quickly as I could, but it wasn't enough. The subordinate server rooms were already compromised.
Even now, every corrupted server room is trying to break through the physical locks that keep them sealed and release all the Corrupted trapped inside.
The Red Tide has reached the ocean. "Erhorn", your enemy, will break into those data centers sooner or later. It's only a matter of time before they're exposed to the world again.
"Helio", will you help me destroy those server rooms? Destroy those children of sin?
NORTHERN WATERS, TRANSATLANTIC ECONOMIC COMMUNITY TERRITORY
LOCATION: KURONO VESSEL, SHIP CABIN. NORTHERN WATERS, TRANSATLANTIC ECONOMIC COMMUNITY TERRITORY.
You've got to be kidding me!
Clausen slams his hand on the table, shock and panic flooding his eyes.
You just told me Moses wasn't an awakened machine!

I said Moses wasn't. I never said the others weren't. As the data integration hub, the Netherweb's processing power and structure make it far more susceptible to developing autonomous consciousness than the other modules.

Do you have any idea what awakened machines mean? How much destruction they've caused? Calling them enemies of humanity, right up there with the Punishing Virus, wouldn't be much of a stretch. If an entire node has awakened...

The scenario you're fearing won't happen, Captain. The awakened machines of the Millennium Project hold no hostility toward humanity. Truth be told, they couldn't care less about what happens on the surface.

There are reports that awakened machines are still shaped by their pre-awakening programs... Anyway. Lieutenant Colonel, you said it asked you a favor. Did you go through with it? Destroy the other server rooms?
I did. I used the Netherweb's data to locate every server room packed with the Corrupted...
But while I was destroying them, the chain reaction caught the measurement equipment scattered across the seafloor. That's what caused the explosion on the surface.
Tsk... You're an instructor, for god's sake. Don't you know how to manage risk in underwater combat?
My gear wasn't configured for deep-sea operations. What you saw was the best I could do to keep the damage contained.
Hmph, fine. So did you clear out all the corrupted server rooms or not?
Every last one. Once the threats were eliminated, I returned to the Netherweb. It initiated the connection to the master AI immediately.
它能自己连入主脑的啊?
Given its function as a data center, it has more capabilities than the other modules. The only reason it hadn't connected sooner was the corrupted server rooms under its jurisdiction.
So where exactly is this master AI? Look, Lieutenant Colonel, your premature actions did cause us considerable trouble...
But if we can secure the master AI, it'll make my report to command look a lot prettier. As for everything you pulled out there, consider it settled.
在幽网成功连接以后，我就立刻和主脑取得了完整的联系，得知了其所在位置。
Seventeen thousand meters beneath the ocean surface. That's where the master AI, Abyss Passer, is right now.
It's been waiting there for ten years.
